blocks.title: 1. What Is an Angle?
blocks.content:
An angle measures a **turn** between two lines that meet at a point.

We measure angles in **degrees (°)**. A full circle all the way around is **360°**.

blocks.title: 2. The Angle Family
blocks.content:
**Acute (< 90°)** angles are small and sharp — like a half-open book.

**Right (90°)** angles make a perfect L-shape [ ∟ ].

**Obtuse (> 90°)** angles are wide and open — past the right angle.

**Straight (180°)** angles look like a flat line — no bend at all.

blocks.title: 3. Angle Rules
blocks.content:
**Angles on a straight line add up to 180°.** If one angle is 110°, the other must be 70° because together they make a straight line.

**Vertically opposite angles are equal.** When two lines cross, the angles sitting opposite each other are always the same size.

blocks.title: 4. Example
blocks.content:
Two angles sit on a straight line. One is **135°**.

**Step 1:** A straight line equals 180°.
**Step 2:** 180° − 135° = 45°.

The missing angle is **45°**.

blocks.title: 5. Pitfalls
blocks.content:
Don't confuse a **straight line (180°)** with a **full circle (360°)**!

Always check whether the angles sit on a line or go all the way around a point — the total changes.
